views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Take the October working-level and ministerial talks without adding new tariffs or rolling back the lists already in force. Keep List 3 at 25% and List 4A at 15% as leverage; treat the announced Oct. 15 hike (25% to 30% on ~$250B) as a contingent threat, not an automatic step, and do not pull List 4B forward from Dec. 15. Press Beijing for enforceable soybean/pork purchase volumes and a written path on IP and forced tech transfer, but do not trade Huawei delisting or a broad tariff rollback for a thin buy-order.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not existential. After List 4A took effect on 2019-09-01 at 15%, combined US Section 301 coverage now reaches the remaining consumer/industrial slice on top of the ~$250B already at 10–25%; China answered with a ~$75B retaliation (including autos) whose first tranche also landed Sept. 1 (timeline 2019-08-23, 2019-08-30, 2019-09-01). Farm-belt exposure is the clearest US interest hit: soy exports to China fell from $12.2B to $3.1B, pork faced stacked duties up to ~72%, and Washington has already spent ~$28B in farm aid (NYT 2019-09-12; CNN 2019-09-11; Politico 2019-09-13). Markets priced that escalation as a growth shock: the 10-year yield fell from 2.43% (late March) to 1.47% around the Aug. 23–Sept. 3 peak, the 2s10s curve inverted in mid-August and again on Aug. 23, and fed funds were cut from 2.42% to 2.04% (country_health DGS10/FEDFUNDS; CNBC/USA Today Aug. 14–23). That sits between the USA +0.0 and +0.5 anchors — material GDP/political drag and a key export sector exposed, not a supply-chain or tech-leadership collapse. Huawei remains on the Entity List (2019-05-16) and List 4B (phones, laptops, toys) was deliberately delayed to Dec. 15 to protect the holiday season (2019-08-13), which is itself evidence that further consumer-facing escalation is costly at home.

Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. The May 5 hike after China was seen to “renegotiate,” the July 30 Shanghai “little progress” round, and the Aug. 1–23 tariff cascade produced inversion and retaliation, then a mid-September thaw: China’s 16-category industrial/chemical exemptions (2019-09-11), soy/pork exclusion from additional duties plus reported boatload soybean inquiries (2019-09-13), and the US delay of the Oct. 1 hike to Oct. 15 at Liu He’s request for the PRC 70th anniversary (NYT 2019-09-12; Politico 2019-09-13). Working-level talks are teed for the coming week and Lighthizer/Mnuchin–Liu He talks for early October. A further hike now would likely recreate the August market shock and invite more farm/auto retaliation; a rollback or purchase-only concession would cash in leverage before the enforcement/IP/SOE issues that broke talks in May are even back on paper. An interim farm-purchase package can be explored at the table, but it is not yet a matching offer that would justify concede_purchases.
key_factors: List 4A (15%) already live; Oct. 15 25→30% hike still hanging as unused leverage
Farm-belt retaliation: soy collapse, stacked pork duties, ~$28B aid, 2020 political exposure
August yield-curve inversion and Fed easing show the dispute is biting US financial conditions
Mid-September goodwill (China farm/industrial exemptions; US two-week hike delay) and October talks
Structural/enforcement/IP issues still unresolved after May breakdown and July Shanghai stalemate
Huawei Entity List and List 4B (holiday consumer goods) are separate levers, not chips to give away pre-talks

sources_cited.excerpt: List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods (5–10%, split Sept 1 / Dec 15), including re-imposing tariffs on US autos. Trump orders US companies to "immediately start looking for an alternative to China" and directs a 5-point increase on the planned List 4 rate (to 15%).
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
US 10-year yield latest 1.80 on 2019-09-18; change -0.63 (-25.9%) over the window, with a trough of 1.47 around 2019-08-28 to 2019-09-04.
Federal funds effective rate latest 2.04% (2019-09-01), down from 2.42% in April (change -0.38, -15.7%).

Trump delayed the next tariff increase by two weeks to Oct. 15 after China announced limited exemptions; he said China would buy large amounts of US agricultural products. Talks planned for early October; deep divisions remain; Mnuchin said the delay was a goodwill gesture at Liu He's request over the Oct. 1 70th anniversary.

Xinhua: China will exclude soybeans, pork and other farm goods from additional tariffs and allow purchases of a 'certain amount' of US farm products, in response to the US postponement of the $250B rate hike from Oct. 1 to Oct. 15. Analysts called it a possible narrow/interim deal, not a structural settlement.
China's first exemption list did not cover soy/pork. Soy exports to China fell to $3.1B in 2018 from $12.2B; Trump has directed $28B in farm aid. Farmers are a political headache for the White House.

On Aug. 14 the 2-year/10-year Treasury yields inverted for the first time since before the Great Recession; longer-term yields had been falling on anxiety that the trade war could derail the global economy.
